This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them. Original: 60.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz. Original: 20.
Borg runs at 4 MHz = 250 ns. 40 ns (25 MHz) caused post-CTS resizer to overflow die (DPL-0036).
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
CLOCK_UNCERTAINTY_CONSTRAINT (default 0.25, unset here) plus these two
margins matched exactly what TinyTapeout/tinytapeout-ihp-25a-sources'
actually-submitted tt_um_MichaelBell_tinyQV uses (0.25/0.1/0.05, at
80 MHz -- 20x our clock, so proportionally a much harder bar). Briefly
tried lowering CLOCK_UNCERTAINTY_CONSTRAINT to 0.05 to chase the
post-CTS hold-violation rate (RSZ-0046: 8500/8615 flops, 98.7%) down
to 8; reverted -- that real proven-tapeout reference makes it much
more likely that was removing legitimate margin than fixing a bug.
tinyQV's die is ~1/8th Borg's (508.76x225.76um vs 1289.28x710.64um)
with far fewer flops, so it credibly meets the same margin on a
smaller/better clock tree where Borg's larger one can't. Register-
count reduction (validated: 1202->279 DPL-0036 failures from one RTL
cut) is the legitimate lever here, not this constraint.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
